newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a deal announced yesterday, Telstra and News Corp have negotiated a settlement to their pay-TV business dealings. News Corp has agreed to limit Telstra's giant cable rollout to under 3 million homes, and Telstra will pay News Corp up to A$100 million in compensation. Page 1.

The author of the influential 1989 report Australia and the Northeast Asian Ascendancy, Professor Ross Garnaut, has criticised the Federal Government's recent decision to freeze car tariffs until early next century. Speaking at the Federation of Automotive Products Manufacturers convention yesterday, he said the decision was "a symptom and an omen of a serious national malaise". Page 1.

The domestic computer retail industry is planning to target a new market segment of price-sensitive buyers. In preparation for expected sharp competition later this year from brand-name personal computers retailers are hoping that computer companies can produce PCs able to be sold for $1,500. Page 1

The Prime Minister John Howard again urged tax reform yesterday with his call being strongly backed by Coalition MPs. Speaking at a specifically convened meeting of Coaliton members Howard, supported by Treasurer Peter Costello, stressed the need for urgent tax reform, primarily in the shape of a GST, in order to promote economic growth. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A joint study released yesterday by Citibank and the Real Estate Institute of Australia, which compares family income with average home loan repayments, reveals that low interest rates have made home-loan affordability reach its highest since September 1994. This is despite rising house prices across Australia. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello last night launched the Government's official campaign for an overhaul of the national taxation system. Speaking at a special meeting of Coalition backbenchers, Costello linked the lack of employment growth with the existing tax system. Page 1.

Independent Senator Mal Colston has outmanoeuvred Prime Minister John Howard's ban on the Government accepting his vote in the Senate. In a surprise move yesterday Senator Colston sat with the Government to vote against a Labor amendment to the Custom Exise Bill and Government whip Paul Calvert, apparently forgetting the Prime Minister's instructions, counted his vote in the final tally. Page 1.

The Opposition, the Australian Democrats and the Greens yesterday declared they would not pass the Government's proposal for a voluntary postal vote for electing delegates to the Constitutional Convention on Australia through the Senate. The Senate opposition parties are calling for compulsory voting and say their position is non-negotiable. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The proposed 10 per cent bed tax on NSW hotels has caused a division between the State Government and Sydney 2000 Olympic organisers. Australian Olympic Committee head John Coates began lobbying against the tax yesterday, saying it would jeopardise approximately A$500 million in sponsorship. Page 1.

Film Australia's managing director Bruce Moir confirmed last night that an investigation has begun into discrepancies in the organisation's accounts. The discovery of financial irregularities by auditors last Wednesday coincided with the departure of a senior executive. Page 1.

Federal Peter Costello last night stressed the need for a rapid imposition of a GST, claiming the current erosion of the indirect tax base would result in ordinary Australians being pushed into higher tax-brackets. Addressing a special meeting of Coalition MPs and Senators Costello reaffirmed the Government's commitment to tax reform. Page 1.

NSW Rail has ordered a freeze on all "non-essential" expenditure in an attempt to overcome a A$100 million cutback in Government funding announced in last month's State Budget. An internal memo reveals the organisation will face a A$25 million cash shortall at the end of the financial year. Page 2.
THE AGE

Victorian police will today intensify search efforts for a 14-month old toddler, missing since the weekend in the La Trobe valley. Jaydn Leskie disappeared between 2am and 3am on Sunday after being left alone in a house by his stepfather who went to collct his mother from a nearby hotel. Page A1.

The inquiry into the 1991 death of Melinda Freemen, 26, who was found bashed to death in her home, heard yesterday that her husband had told a former lover they could be together only if Mrs Freemen was dead. The comment was made by Pamela Gilmore, a former lover of Craig Freeman. Page A1.

In an interview with London's Financial Times newspaper, Prime Minister John Howard denied accusations that Australia was in danger of entering a new state of economic isolationism, blaming Australia's media for promoting negative images. Mr Howard made the comments in advance of his tour of the UK and US which begins today. Page A1.

Prime Minister John Howard has confirmed the Government's strong support for a complete overhaul of the tax system. Speaking last night at a special meeting of Coalition ministers and backbenchers he put forward the case for tax reform in an attempt to secure party room support before he leaves for an overseas trip today. Page A2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
